title: Hazardous materials and substances
summary: Covers hazardous substances, CLP hazard signs and packaging rules, the hazards and precautions for solvents and lubricants, and the scope of the COSHH regulations.

sections.heading: Hazardous substances and CLP
paragraphs: A hazardous substance is something that can cause ill-health to people at work. Under the CLP regulations, manufacturers of any hazardous substance must identify the specific hazards the substance poses.

The packaging must be suitable to contain the substance safely, both in transit and in storage, and must carry clear labelling with warning signs and safety advice. CLP uses hazard signs (sometimes called pictograms) so that the hazards of materials and substances can be identified quickly.
bullets: Hazardous substance: something that can cause ill-health to people at work
Manufacturers must identify the specific hazards of the substance
Labels must carry warning signs and safety advice
CLP hazard signs are also called pictograms

sections.heading: Solvents
paragraphs: Solvents are substances that dissolve a chemically different liquid, solid or gas, resulting in a solution. A solvent is usually a liquid but can also be a solid or a gas.
Many solvents are hazardous materials, so take general precautions when using them.
bullets: Hazards: normally flammable or highly flammable, explosive, toxic, fumes that can cause unconsciousness and death, carcinogenic, and environmental effects
Keep storage containers tightly closed
Never use open flames near flammable solvents; use electrical heating instead
Never flush solvents down the drain; read safety data sheets for disposal information
Avoid inhaling solvent vapours
Avoid skin contact: many solvents are easily absorbed through the skin, dry the skin and may cause sores and wounds

sections.heading: Lubricants
paragraphs: Lubricants are substances introduced to reduce friction between moving surfaces. They carry their own hazards and need similar care to solvents.
bullets: Hazards: slip hazard when spilt on surfaces, dermatitis, and flammability
Never use open flames near flammable lubricants
Never flush lubricants down the drain; read safety data sheets for disposal information
Avoid skin contact by wearing gloves or barrier cream

sections.heading: Packaging requirements
paragraphs: The CLP regulations set out what packaging for hazardous chemicals must do.
bullets: Prevent escape of the chemical
Not be adversely affected by the chemical
Be strong enough to withstand normal handling
If it has a replaceable closure, continue to prevent escape even after repeated use

sections.heading: COSHH regulations
paragraphs: COSHH stands for the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations. They cover all substances used in the workplace that could be considered hazardous to health and contain detailed information on each type of substance.
Substances covered include chemicals, cements, oils, sprays, etc.
bullets: COSHH = Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations
Covers all workplace substances that could be hazardous to health
Examples: chemicals, cements, oils, sprays

flashcards.back: Something that can cause ill-health to people at work.

flashcards.front: What must manufacturers do under the CLP regulations?
flashcards.back: Identify the specific hazards posed by any hazardous substance, and supply suitable packaging with clear labelling, warning signs and safety advice.

flashcards.front: What are CLP hazard signs sometimes called?
flashcards.back: Pictograms. They help with quick identification of the hazards presented by materials and substances.
A substance that dissolves a chemically different liquid, solid or gas, resulting in a solution. Usually a liquid, but can be a solid or a gas.

flashcards.front: List hazards that solvents can present.
flashcards.back: Flammable or highly flammable, explosive, toxic, fumes causing unconsciousness and death, carcinogenic, and environmental effects.

flashcards.front: What should you use instead of open flames near flammable solvents?
Where can you find proper disposal information for solvents and lubricants?
flashcards.back: In the safety data sheets. Never flush them down the drain.

flashcards.front: Why must skin contact with solvents be avoided?
flashcards.back: Many solvents are easily absorbed through the skin. They also dry the skin and may cause sores and wounds.
A substance introduced to reduce friction between moving surfaces.

flashcards.front: What are the hazards of lubricants?
flashcards.back: Slip hazard when spilt on surfaces, dermatitis, and flammability.

flashcards.front: How should you protect your skin from lubricants?
flashcards.back: Avoid contact by wearing gloves or barrier cream.

flashcards.front: What four things must CLP packaging do?
flashcards.back: Prevent escape of the chemical, not be adversely affected by it, be strong enough for normal handling, and (with a replaceable closure) keep preventing escape after repeated use.

flashcards.front: What does COSHH stand for and what does it cover?
flashcards.back: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations. It covers all workplace substances that could be hazardous to health, such as chemicals, cements, oils and sprays.

quiz.q: Which regulations require manufacturers of hazardous substances to identify the specific hazards and label the packaging?
quiz.why: Under the CLP regulations, manufacturers must identify the hazards and provide suitable packaging with clear labelling, warning signs and safety advice.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of CLP hazard signs (pictograms)?
options: To show the price of a substance
To explain how to dispose of waste
To help with quick identification of the hazards of materials and substances
To show who made the substance
quiz.why: CLP hazard signs help with the quick identification of hazards presented by materials and substances.

options: A substance that reduces friction between moving surfaces
A substance that dissolves a chemically different liquid, solid or gas, resulting in a solution
A substance that only exists as a gas
quiz.why: A solvent dissolves a chemically different liquid, solid or gas to give a solution; it is usually, but not always, a liquid.

quiz.q: You need to heat a container near a flammable solvent. Which is the correct precaution?
options: Use a lit torch at a distance
Leave the container open to let vapours escape
quiz.why: Never use open flames near flammable solvents; use electrical heating instead.

quiz.q: How should unwanted solvent be disposed of?
options: According to the safety data sheet's disposal information
quiz.why: Never flush solvents down the drain; read the safety data sheets for proper disposal information.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid skin contact with solvents?
options: They are easily absorbed through the skin and dry it, which may cause sores and wounds
They only affect the skin when cold
quiz.why: Many solvents are easily absorbed through the skin and also dry it, which may cause sores and wounds.

quiz.q: Which hazard is specific to spilt lubricants on surfaces?
quiz.why: Lubricants present a slip hazard when spilt, as well as dermatitis and flammability.

quiz.q: How can you reduce the risk of dermatitis from lubricants?
options: Use an open flame to warm the lubricant
Flush skin contact areas with solvent
Store the lubricant in an open tub
quiz.why: Avoid contact by the lubricant with the skin by wearing gloves or barrier cream.

quiz.q: Which of these is a CLP requirement for packaging of a chemical?
options: It must be strong enough to withstand normal handling
It must be disposable after one use
quiz.why: CLP requires packaging to prevent escape, not be affected by the chemical, withstand normal handling, and keep sealing after repeated use of any replaceable closure.

quiz.q: A replaceable closure on a hazardous chemical's container must do what?
options: Continue to prevent escape even after repeated use
quiz.why: If the package has a replaceable closure, it must continue to prevent escape even after repeated use.

quiz.q: Which regulations cover all substances used in the workplace that could be hazardous to health, including cements, oils and sprays?
quiz.why: COSHH (Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations) covers chemicals, cements, oils, sprays and other hazardous substances.
